chunks: Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn ʿĪsā, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn al-Mughīrah, from Ismāʿīl ibn Abī Ziyād, from Jaʿfar, from his father عليهما السلام, that Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام said:

Concerning a woman who claimed that she menstruated three times in a single month, he said: “Assign women from her close associates to verify that her menstruation in the past was as she claimed. If they testify, she has spoken the truth; otherwise, she is lying.”
And this report does not contradict that.

key_terms.امْرَأَةٍ: a woman involved in the legal question
key_terms.بِطَانَتِهَا: her close associates or women intimately familiar with her condition
key_terms.شَهْرٍ: a month, the time period under discussion
key_terms.كَاذِبَةٌ: deemed untruthful if the claim is not corroborated
key_terms.نِسْوَةً: women called upon to verify the claim

ai.seo_question: How is a woman’s claim of having three menstrual cycles in one month verified in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a legal claim made by a woman regarding the occurrence of three menstrual cycles within one month. It instructs that women familiar with her condition and past habit should be consulted; if they confirm her claim, it is accepted, and if not, it is rejected.
